newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-RAI STEALS LAST GASP WINNER FOR PSG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAI STEALS LAST GASP WINNER FOR PSG.

text.p: Former Brazil captain Rai snatched an 88th minute winner as Paris St Germain came from two goals down to beat 10-man Auxerre 3-2 away in the French first division on Thursday.

PSG's French international striker Florian Maurice scored a 73rd minute equaliser eight minutes after Auxerre, who lost their opening match 3-0 at Lens on Saturday, had left back Franck Rabarivony sent off for a second bookable offence.
The result put PSG three points clear of the field, most of whom are in action on Friday. It also left 1995 champions Auxerre at the foot of the table.
PSG fell two goals behind in the first half to a header from striker Stephane Guivarch, the league's top scorer last season when he played for Rennes, and a volley by winger Steve Marlet.
PSG looked more determined in the second half and Italian striker Marco Simone pulled one back with his first league goal for the Parisians nine minutes after the interval.
PSG thought they had equalised two minutes later but the goal was disallowed for offside after a long discussion between the referee, who had given a goal at first, and his linesman.

This merely served for PSG to increase the pressure. Rabarivony was sent off after arguing and minutes later Maurice turned on a loose ball to equalise with his second goal in two games. Rai then settled the match for the visitors.
Lyon, who lost forwards Florian Maurice and Franck Gava to PSG in the close season, won 3-0 at Rennes with goals by Alain Caveglia, Christophe Delmotte and Joseph-Desire Job.
